judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Contract Time as the period 'including authorized adjustments, allotted in the Contract Documents, for Substantial Completion'. Definite as a definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 4.3, whose day-count is incomplete, and First Addendum 4.3 [Revised], which substitutes a fixed calendar date; a 'period of time' definition does not map cleanly onto a fixed end date with a conditional start. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The date of commencement of the Work is the date established in the Agreement.' A pure pointer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 4.1 ('Approximately the Fifteenth of July') and First Addendum 4.1 [Revised] ('July 15, 2002, pending approval of permits'); the Agreement does not establish a firm date, so the definition has no fixed referent. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The date of Substantial Completion is the date certified by the Architect under 9.8. A pointer with a defined certifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.8.4 and First Addendum 4.4 (bonus keyed to the 'established date of Substantial Completion'); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Day' means calendar day 'unless otherwise specifically defined'. Clear default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.2.2, which uses 'five (5) business days', and Agreement 4.3's 'calendar days'; the default is displaced where the documents say so. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Time limits stated in the Contract Documents are of the essence of the Contract', with the Contractor confirming the Contract Time is reasonable. Strong but definite language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 4.3, where the liquidated damages and bonus insert was left blank, First Addendum 4.4 (an undetermined bonus) and 4.1 (commencement 'pending approval of permits'); time is declared of the essence in a schedule that is itself indeterminate. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bars knowing premature commencement before insurance is effective and requires five days' notice before commencing 'unless the date of commencement is established by the Contract Documents or a notice to proceed'. The conditions are stated but the OCR runs 8.2.2 and 8.2.3 together here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 4.1, whose Owner time-requirement for filing mortgages and mechanic's liens was left blank, and 2.1.2; the notice mechanism this clause assumes was never completed. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proceed expeditiously with adequate forces' and achieve Substantial Completion within the Contract Time. 'Expeditiously' and 'adequate forces' are open but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 4.3/First Addendum 4.3 and 8.2.1; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extends the Contract Time for an enumerated list of causes and then adds 'or other causes beyond the Contractor's control' and 'or by other causes which the Architect determines may justify delay' — two successive catch-alls after a specific list, with the extension left to 'such reasonable time as the Architect may determine'. The general-versus-specific problem is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.4 (no separate increase for concurrent or interrelated causes) and 4.3.7.1-4.3.7.3; the supplements narrow an entitlement whose outer boundary this clause deliberately leaves open. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Claims relating to time shall be made in accordance with applicable provisions of Paragraph 4.3.' A pure routing sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.7 and Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contract Sum is stated in the Agreement and, including authorized adjustments, is the total amount payable by the Owner to the Contractor.' The definition asserts a fact about the Agreement rather than defining a computation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.1.1 (Contract Sum is the Cost of the Work plus the Fee, with no figure) and 5.2.1 (GMP 'N/A'); no sum is stated in the Agreement at all, so a defined term used throughout Article 9, Article 11 and Article 14 has no fixed content. Serious incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires an itemised Application 'at least ten days before the date established for each progress payment', notarised if required, supported by 'such data substantiating the Contractor's right to payment as the Owner or Architect may require'. The open-ended data requirement is the soft point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.3, whose application and payment dates are blank or garbled, and 12.1.4/First Addendum 12.1.4; the ten-day lead time runs from a date the Agreement never fixed. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits Applications to include amounts authorized by Construction Change Directives or interim determinations. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.3.8 and Supplementary Conditions 7.2.3; consistent, though the supplement's final-settlement rule sits nearby. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions payment for stored materials on 'procedures satisfactory to the Owner to establish the Owner's title ... or otherwise protect the Owner's interest'. A satisfaction standard with no reasonableness qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 7.5.6 and 12.1.7.2, which use advance approval and a written location agreement; the two describe the same subject with different conditions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A title warranty qualified by 'to the best of the Contractor's knowledge, information and belief' as to freedom from liens. The knowledge qualifier on a warranty is a familiar arguable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.4(b) (lien waivers for amounts of $2,500 or more) and 9.10.2; the qualified warranty and the documentary waivers do different work. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Architect to issue a Certificate or state reasons for withholding 'within seven days after receipt' of the Application. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.3, which says its own time periods 'supersede those stated in Subparagraph 9.4.1', and against Agreement 12.1.3; this provision is expressly displaced for final accounting purposes. Real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully hedged statement of what a Certificate does and does not represent, with four express disclaimers. Detailed but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.9, which makes the same disclaimers, and 9.5.1; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits withholding 'to the extent reasonably necessary to protect the Owner' on an enumerated list ending with 'persistent failure to carry out the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents', and includes 'reasonable evidence that the Work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum'. 'Persistent', 'reasonably necessary' and 'reasonable evidence' are all nameable, and the list is closed rather than illustrative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.1.1/5.2.1, where there is no stated Contract Sum or GMP against which to test whether the Work 'can be completed for the unpaid balance', and against 12.1.7.6. Real difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When the above reasons for withholding certification are removed, certification will be made for amounts previously withheld.' Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.5.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Owner shall pay 'in the manner and within the time provided in the Contract Documents'. Entirely referential.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.3, whose payment-day fill-ins are blank or garbled, and First Addendum 12.2.2; the time it points to was never fixed for progress payments. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prompt pay-through obligation to Subcontractors reflecting retained percentages, with a flow-down requirement. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.8 (subcontractor retainage of not less than 10%) and First Addendum 12.1.7.3 (5% on the Fee); the retainage figures differ but apply to different amounts. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: No Owner or Architect obligation to pay Subcontractors 'except as may otherwise be required by law'. Clear with a statutory saving.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 9.6.2.1, which lets the Owner make joint payments while disclaiming any obligation or rights in the subcontractor; consistent in effect. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Treats material suppliers in a manner 'similar' to Subcontractors. 'Similar' is loose but the reference is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.6.2-9.6.4 and Supplementary Conditions 9.6.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A non-acceptance rule for payment, partial use or occupancy. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.9.3 and 9.10.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires payments to be 'held by the Contractor' for Subcontractors while expressly denying any separate account, fiduciary liability, tort liability or punitive damages. Creating a holding obligation and then disclaiming every consequence of it is an odd construction, though deliberately drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.6.2 (pay-through duty) and Supplementary Conditions 9.6.2.1 (joint checks); the disclaimers sit consistently with the no-privity structure. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stop-work right if the Architect does not certify within seven days 'or if the Owner does not pay the Contractor within seven days after the date established in the Contract Documents', with the Contract Sum increased by shutdown, delay and start-up costs 'plus interest as provided for in the Contract Documents'. The trigger is precise only if the underlying date is.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.3 (payment dates blank or garbled), First Addendum 12.2.2 and Agreement 14.2 (interest rate line left blank); a powerful stop-work remedy hangs on two dates and a rate the Contract Documents never fixed. Real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substantial Completion is 'the stage ... when the Work ... is sufficiently complete in accordance with the Contract Documents so that the Owner can occupy or utilize the Work for its intended use'. 'Sufficiently complete' and 'intended use' are the classic disputed terms on a residence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 4.3 (fixed date), 4.4 (bonus for early completion) and First Addendum 12.2.1 (recorded Notice of Completion); the definition drives a bonus, a deadline and final payment. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a 'comprehensive list of items to be completed or corrected', with omission not altering the obligation to complete. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.8.3-9.8.4 and 12.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inspection procedure with a re-inspection loop if items are 'not sufficiently complete'. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.8.1 and 9.8.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Certificate 'shall establish the date of Substantial Completion' and fix responsibilities for security, maintenance, utilities, damage and insurance, and warranties commence then 'unless otherwise provided in the Certificate'. Delegating those allocations to a future certificate leaves the allocation open until it is issued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 4.3/4.4, 9.8.5 and 12.2.2 (one-year correction period running from Substantial Completion); several consequences turn on a document whose content is discretionary. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: On acceptance and surety consent 'the Owner shall make payment of retainage applying to such Work', adjusted for incomplete or nonconforming Work. Clear mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.7.3, where retainage on the Fee is 'N/A', First Addendum 12.1.7.3 (5%) and Agreement 12.1.8 (10% for Subcontractors); what retainage is payable depends on which of the conflicting figures governs. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A joint inspection before partial occupancy to record the condition of the Work. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.9.3 and 11.4.1.5 (insurer consent to partial occupancy); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Partial occupancy is not acceptance of noncomplying Work 'unless otherwise agreed upon'. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.6.6 and 9.9.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A final inspection and certification procedure with the Architect certifying that the Work has been completed and 'the entire balance found to be due the Contractor ... is due and payable'. Detailed and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.3 (whose time periods supersede 9.4.1 and which routes the final accounting through the Owner's accountants), Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 (Owner acceptance of warranties) and First Addendum 12.2.1/12.2.2; four documents describe the final-payment gateway differently. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of five submittals closing with '(5) if required by the Owner, other data establishing payment or satisfaction of obligations ... to the extent and in such form as may be designated by the Owner'. A wholly Owner-defined residual item after a specific list is a general-versus-specific point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.4(b)/12.2.1/12.2.2 and Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1; the conditions on final payment accumulate across documents without a single controlling list. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits partial payment where final completion is 'materially delayed through no fault of the Contractor', with such payment not constituting a waiver of claims. 'Materially delayed' is the soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.10.4 (making of final payment as waiver) and Agreement 12.2.2/First Addendum 12.2.2; the non-waiver carve-out is consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Final payment waives all Owner Claims 'except those arising from' three enumerated categories, including 'failure of the Work to comply with the requirements of the Contract Documents'. The third exception is broad enough that the scope of the waiver is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.10 (consequential damages waiver), 12.2.5 (obligations not limited by the correction period) and 13.7.1; several overlapping waiver and limitation provisions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Acceptance of final payment waives all claims 'except those previously made in writing and identified by that payee as unsettled at the time of final Application for Payment'. The identification requirement is a strict, easily missed condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.4 (30-day arbitration demand or the accountants' figure becomes binding) and 4.3.2's 21-day rule; three separate forfeiture mechanisms bear on the same claims. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contractor shall be responsible for initiating, maintaining and supervising all safety precautions and programs.' Clear and absolute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1, which disclaims Owner responsibility for safety notwithstanding the Owner's expanded approval rights; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable precautions' and 'reasonable protection' against damage to three enumerated categories of persons and property. Conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.2.2-10.2.3 and 3.18.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A compliance-with-safety-law obligation. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.7.2 and 10.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable safeguards ... as required by existing conditions and performance of the Contract', with an illustrative list. Ordinary softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.2.1-10.2.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires 'utmost care' where explosives or 'other hazardous materials or equipment or unusual methods' are necessary; the text is truncated here and 'unusual methods' is undefined. Both the truncation and the standard are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.3.1-10.3.3 (hazardous materials) and 3.3.1; the provisions overlap without conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires designation of a responsible safety member, presumed to be the superintendent. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.9.1 and First Addendum Article 2 [Revised], which requires one designated supervisory employee for the project; the two designations may or may not be the same person. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not load or permit any part of the construction or site to be loaded so as to endanger its safety.' Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Triggered where 'reasonable precautions will be inadequate to prevent foreseeable bodily injury or death' from a material 'including but not limited to asbestos or polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)' — an illustrative list attached to a predictive standard. Both elements are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.3.2-10.3.3 and 10.4; the scheme is internally consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed procedure for verification, objection to proposed persons, resumption of Work on written agreement, and equitable adjustment of Time and Sum for shutdown, delay and start-up. Long but concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1 (changes only by Change Order) and Agreement 5.2.1 (GMP 'N/A'); an automatic Contract Sum increase sits alongside a strict Change-Order-only rule. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An Owner indemnity 'to the fullest extent permitted by law' conditioned on the material in fact presenting the described risk and 'provided that such damage, loss or expense is not due to the sole negligence of a party seeking indemnity'. The sole-negligence proviso is the arguable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.18.1 (Contractor's indemnity, which is proportionate rather than sole-negligence based) and 10.4; the two indemnities use different fault tests for mirror-image obligations. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes Owner responsibility for materials 'brought to the site by the Contractor unless such materials or substances were required by the Contract Documents'. Clear allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.3.1-10.3.3 and 3.5; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: In an emergency the Contractor 'shall act, at the Contractor's discretion, to prevent threatened damage, injury or loss', with compensation determined under 4.3 and Article 7. A discretion-plus-duty formulation, but clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 7.7.2 [Revision], which reimburses emergency costs 'only to the extent not ... capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition', and against Agreement 7.7.2; the Addendum materially narrows the compensation this clause preserves. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eight-item enumeration of claims to be insured against, with no limits stated in the clause itself. Precise as a list of coverages.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 16, which is entirely blank as to required limits of liability and bonds, and against 11.1.2; the enumeration is unaccompanied by any figure anywhere in the Contract Documents. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Insurance must be 'written for not less than limits of liability specified in the Contract Documents or required by law, whichever coverage is greater', maintained without interruption to final payment. The comparison rule is clear if both inputs exist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 16 (blank) and Exhibit E (a certificate of insurance offering evidence only); no limits are specified anywhere, so one side of the 'whichever is greater' test is missing. Real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires certificates 'acceptable to the Owner' filed before commencement, with 30 days' notice of cancellation and continuation certificates 'if reasonably available'. 'Acceptable to the Owner' and 'reasonably available' are the soft terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit E (the certificate of insurance in the Contract Documents, which itself says it 'confers no rights' and 'does not amend, extend or alter the coverage'), and against Article 16; the certificate cannot supply the missing requirements. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner shall be responsible for purchasing and maintaining the Owner's usual liability insurance' — 'usual' is undefined and Owner-specific, so the obligation has no ascertainable content. Nameable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 11.6 (cost-shifting for failure to purchase or maintain insurance 'required under Article 11') and Article 16 (blank); the cost-shifting rule attaches to an obligation with no measurable content. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Optionally, the Owner may require' this coverage, with reimbursement by increasing the Contract Sum, and minimum limits 'equal to the aggregate of the limits required for Contractor's Liability Insurance under Clauses 11.1.1.2 through 11.1.1.5'. The referenced limits do not exist here, so the minimum cannot be computed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.18.1, whose indemnity applies only 'to the extent claims ... are not covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance', and against Article 16 (blank); the indemnity's carve-out depends on optional coverage that was apparently never required. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A waiver of rights among Owner, Contractor and Architect 'to the extent damages are covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance'. Conditional and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.3.1 (the coverage is optional and none appears to have been required) and 3.18.1; a waiver keyed to non-existent coverage is inert but not contradictory. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner shall not require the Contractor to include the Owner, Architect or other persons or entities as additional insureds on the Contractor's Liability Insurance coverage under Subparagraph 11.1.1.' A clear prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit E's certificate of insurance and Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1/11.6; the Supplementary Conditions do not override this prohibition, though Owner-side insurance expectations run through several provisions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires property insurance 'in the amount of the initial Contract Sum plus value of subsequent Contract modifications and cost of materials supplied or installed by others'. The measure is precise only if an initial Contract Sum exists.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.1.1 (Contract Sum is Cost of the Work plus Fee, no figure) and 5.2.1 (GMP 'N/A'), and A201 9.1.1; there is no 'initial Contract Sum' to insure to. Serious relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated all-risk coverage list 'including, without limitation' a series of named perils. The 'without limitation' opener makes the list illustrative, which is deliberate rather than defective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.4.1 and Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1 (tools and construction equipment excluded); consistent as a narrowing. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: If the Owner does not intend to purchase the coverage it must so inform the Contractor in writing before commencement, failing which it bears 'all reasonable costs properly attributable thereto'. Clear conditions and consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 11.6, which states a parallel but reciprocal cost-shifting rule, and 11.4.1; two overlapping rules for the same failure. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If the property insurance requires deductibles, the Owner shall pay costs not covered because of such deductibles.' Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.4.1, which in this text describes the policy as written 'without optional deductibles'; whether deductibles are permitted at all is stated inconsistently. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This property insurance shall cover portions of the Work stored off the site, and also portions of the Work in transit.' Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1 (tools and construction equipment on site excluded) and Agreement 7.5.6/12.1.7.2; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions partial occupancy on insurer consent and requires both parties to take 'reasonable steps' and take no action that would cause cancellation or reduction. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.9.1-9.9.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boiler and machinery insurance 'required by the Contract Documents or by law', with Owner and Contractor as named insureds. The requirement is conditional on a specification elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 16, which is blank, so nothing is 'required by the Contract Documents'; the obligation is contingent on a specification that was never made. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Owner 'at the Owner's option, may purchase and maintain' loss-of-use insurance, yet the next sentence unconditionally waives all rights of action against the Contractor for loss of use 'however caused'. An unconditional waiver attached to optional insurance is a genuine asymmetry on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.10 (mutual consequential damages waiver, which already waives Owner losses of use) and 11.4.7; the waivers overlap and are stated with different conditions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires waiver in accordance with 11.4.7 where the Owner insures adjacent property separately, with endorsements. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.4.7 and 11.4.1; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Owner to file policy copies with the Contractor 'before an exposure to loss may occur' and to include cancellation and reduction notice provisions. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.1.3 (the mirror obligation on the Contractor) and Supplementary Conditions 11.6; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad mutual subrogation waiver extending to consultants and separate contractors, effective 'even though that person or entity would otherwise have a duty of indemnification ... and whether or not the person or entity had an insurable interest'. Its interaction with the indemnity obligations it expressly overrides is a familiar arguable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.18.1 (Contractor's indemnity) and Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1, which requires the Contractor's own equipment policy to include a waiver 'in accordance with the requirements of Paragraph 11.4.7'; the waiver and the indemnity cut against each other. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Loss adjusted by the Owner as fiduciary and payable 'for the insureds, as their interests may appear', subject to mortgagee clauses. Standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.4.7 and 9.6.7; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires prompt correction of rejected or nonconforming Work 'whether discovered before or after Substantial Completion and whether or not fabricated, installed or completed', with costs including additional testing and the Architect's expenses borne by the Contractor. The text is badly damaged here, and the temporal reach of the obligation is exactly what parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.2.2.2/12.2.2.3 (the one-year period), 12.2.5 and 13.7.1; the relationship between the correction period and general liability is addressed in several places with different formulations. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence breaks off mid-clause — 'shall be extended with[out] ... Work first performed after Substantial Completion by the period of time ... Completion and the actual performance of the Work' — so the extension rule cannot be applied as written. That incompleteness is a mechanical defect on the face of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.2.2.1, 12.2.2.3 and 13.7.1; the correction-period arithmetic depends on a sentence that is missing its operative middle. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As it stands the sentence reads 'The one-year period for correction of Work shall not be performed by the Contractor pursuant to this Paragraph 12.2' — which is not a coherent proposition, the words 'be extended by corrective Work' having dropped out. A rule about the running of a limitation period that says the opposite of what it means is a clear mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.2.2.1-12.2.2.2 and 12.2.5; the neighbouring provisions show what was intended, but the text as written contradicts them. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Says the correction obligation is not a limitation on other obligations and that the one-year period 'relates only to the specific obligation of the Contractor to correct the Work' and 'has no relationship to the time within which the obligation to comply with the Contract Documents may be sought to be enforced'. Dense and garbled, but its purpose is stated repeatedly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.7.1 (accrual of statutory limitation periods) and 9.10.4.2 (failure of the Work to comply survives final payment); the three provisions on limitation and correction interlock but not transparently. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contract shall be governed by the law of the place where the Project is located.' Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.5.3 (mediation in the place of the Project) and 4.6.6; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is heavily damaged, but the substance — mutual binding of successors and assigns, no assignment of the Contract as a whole without written consent, and continuing liability if assigned anyway — is conventional. The damage is the main difficulty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.4.1 (contingent assignment of subcontracts, expressly excepted) and 14.2.2.2; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a fragment survives — 'Contract Documents and rights and remedies ... a limitation of duties, obligations, rights and' — so the operative cumulative-remedies rule cannot be read as written. The incompleteness is the defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.4.2 (no waiver by conduct) and 4.3.10/9.10.4-9.10.5; the surrounding waiver provisions depend on knowing whether remedies are cumulative. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reduced to disconnected fragments in this text; the tests-and-inspections obligation and the associated approvals cannot be reconstructed from the words given. The defect is one of incompleteness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 7.6.4 (laboratory fees) and 12.2.1; the cost allocation for testing depends on a provision that is unreadable here. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Architect to observe tests 'promptly and, where practicable, at the normal place of testing'. 'Where practicable' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.5.1-13.5.4 and 4.2.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tests 'shall be made promptly to avoid unreasonable delay in the Work'. Ordinary softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.5.5 and 8.3.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three separate deemed-accrual rules for statutes of limitation keyed to Substantial Completion, the final Certificate for Payment and post-final-payment acts, with the third heavily garbled here. Contractual manipulation of accrual dates is a genuine construction battleground, and this text is hard to read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.6.3 (no arbitration demand after the claim would be time-barred 'as determined pursuant to Paragraph 13.7'), 12.2.5 and 9.10.4; several provisions defer to this one for the outer limit. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits termination if the Work is stopped for 30 consecutive days 'through no act or fault of the Contractor' for four enumerated reasons, including non-payment 'within the time stated in the Contract Documents'. The enumeration is closed; the payment trigger depends on a date fixed elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.3 (payment dates blank or garbled), 2.2.1 (evidence of financial arrangements) and Agreement 13.1, which caps the Contractor's recovery on termination; the trigger and the remedy are set in different documents. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits termination where suspensions or interruptions 'in the aggregate exceed 100 percent of the total number of days scheduled for completion, or 120 days in any 365-day period, whichever is less'. The '100 percent of the total number of days scheduled' formula is awkward and the text is damaged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.3.1 (suspension for convenience) and Agreement 13.4 (suspension adjusting the GMP and Contract Time); the day-count depends on a schedule that is itself uncertain. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination where the Work is stopped for 60 days because the Owner 'has persistently failed to fulfill the Owner's obligations ... with respect to matters important to the progress of the Work'. 'Persistently' and 'matters important to the progress' are both open standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.1.3 (the recovery it points to) and Agreement 13.1, which caps the amount payable under 14.1.3 at the for-cause figure; the entitlement and the cap come from different documents. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four grounds for cause termination — 'persistently or repeatedly refuses or fails to supply enough properly skilled workers or proper materials', 'persistently disregards laws', and the residual 'otherwise is guilty of substantial breach of a provision of the Contract Documents'. 'Persistently or repeatedly', 'enough', 'proper' and the catch-all 'otherwise ... substantial breach' are all nameable, and the catch-all sits against three specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.2 (which caps the amount payable on for-cause termination) and 14.2.2; the grounds and the consequences are consistent even if the grounds are soft. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires Architect certification 'that sufficient cause exists to justify such action' and seven days' notice, then permits three enumerated remedies including finishing 'by whatever reasonable method the Owner may deem expedient'. The certification condition and the reasonable-method standard are the soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.2.1, 5.4.1 (assignment of subcontracts) and Agreement 13.3; the machinery interlocks. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum exceeds costs of finishing the Work ... such excess shall be paid to the Contractor', with the amount 'certified by the Architect upon application'. The arithmetic is clear; its inputs are not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.2, which prescribes a different computation (Cost of the Work to termination plus a ratio-based Fee less previous payments) and caps it by the Guaranteed Maximum Price, and against 9.1.1/5.2.1 where no Contract Sum or GMP is stated. Two incompatible formulas for the same payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits suspension 'without cause ... for such period of time as the Owner may determine'. Unlimited Owner discretion is a one-sided term but plainly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.4, which requires the GMP and Contract Time to be increased on suspension, and 14.1.2 (termination after prolonged suspension); the compensation route depends on a GMP stated as 'N/A'. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner may, at any time, terminate the Contract for the Owner's convenience and without cause.' Short and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.1, which caps the amount payable under A201 14.1.3 at the for-cause figure, and against 14.4.3, which promises overhead and profit on Work not executed; the consequence of exercising this right is described inconsistently. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated duties on receipt of a convenience-termination notice, including ceasing operations 'as directed by the Owner in the notice'. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.3 (assignment of subcontracts as a condition of payment) and 5.4.1; the direction to terminate subcontracts and the Owner's right to take assignment sit close together. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entitles the Contractor to 'payment for Work executed, and costs incurred by reason of such termination, along with reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed'. 'Costs incurred by reason of such termination' and 'reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed' are both open-ended measures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.1, which caps convenience-termination payment at the for-cause amount 'except that the Contractor's Fee shall be calculated as if the Work had been fully completed', and against 4.3.10, whose consequential damages waiver applies 'without limitation, to all consequential damages due to either party's termination in accordance with Article 14'. Three provisions give three different answers on the same payment.
